simulation.mech.9.body: Rules are kept in the project file, never in the OSB; exported storyboards and videos are not affected.
simulation.mech.8.body: In play an event happens on the frame the player actually hits, with their timing error; missed objects raise nothing; pass/fail depends on health. This simulation uses the exact moments the rules give and does not compute health. Beatmap events are approximate for taiko, catch and mania, and spinner bonuses are not raised.
simulation.mech.7.body: Each rule sets one of lazer's values at a moment: a HitSound rule the set of samples just played, a HitObjectHit rule the latest judgement, a Pass/Fail rule whether the player is passing. A beatmap-events rule raises HitSound and HitObjectHit for the shown difficulty as if every object were hit perfectly. Only ticked rules take effect after Confirm; ticking none turns triggers off.
simulation.mech.7: How rules stand for the game
simulation.mech.6.body: They coexist; neither excludes the other. Pass/fail is one global state that starts Passing (taiko starts Failing and turns Passing once health passes half). It decides whether the Pass or the Fail layer is shown, and fires Passing or Failing triggers the moment it changes. HitSound and HitObjectHit triggers fire whatever the state, on sprites of a hidden layer too; when the layer shows again, its sprites look as they should at that moment. Storyboard sounds of a hidden layer do not play.
simulation.mech.5.body: A sprite exists only while its own commands and loops say so: what a trigger does outside that time is not seen, and a sprite with nothing but triggers is never shown. Give it an ordinary command (such as an F at opacity 0) to set when it exists.
simulation.mech.4.body: Each firing schedules the commands again. A newly scheduled command removes every later command of the same property, the sprite's own commands included, and cuts off one of that property still running when it starts. Firing again therefore restarts rather than adds up, and an F in a trigger cancels the sprite's later F commands, such as a fade-out at its end. Triggers do not exclude each other, and the group number is not used.
simulation.mech.3.body: HitSound[normal bank][addition bank][addition][index]. A bank is All, Normal, Soft or Drum; All or nothing means any. With a single bank followed by an addition (HitSoundSoftClap) the bank is the addition's. The number at the end is the custom sample index (the 2 of soft-hitclap2.wav); indexes 0 and 1 have no suffix, so HitSound1 never fires. A slider tick is a HitSound too, and the normal bank does not restrict it.
simulation.mech.2.body:
- HitSound: a hit object is hit and its sound plays, with the whole set of samples played (normal sound, additions, their banks and index).
- HitObjectHit: a successful, scored judgement (not a miss). A slider's head, ticks, repeats and tail count once each.
- Passing / Failing: the moment the pass/fail state changes. Setting the state it already has fires nothing.
The osu! slider tail judgement can occur 36 ms early, after previous nested judgements; its sound stays at the end. Slider ticks and catch droplets take their bank and index from the green line at the slider's start. Catch bananas also raise HitSound, carrying the spinner's normal sample (hitnormal with its bank and index).
simulation.mech.1.body: Commands under T,condition,start,end[,group] do not run on their own. When the game raises an event that meets the condition at a moment inside the [start, end] window (both ends included; left out means no limit), they run once, counting their times from that moment. This simulation follows osu!lazer exactly.

clash.add:
"{0}" and "{1}" cannot be in effect at the same time: they are about the same thing, and osu! lets only one of them have its way at any moment.

At {2} the two would overlap, so nothing was added.

Keep their times apart: add it after the other one has ended (or before it begins), or delete the stretch that overlaps first.
track.blocked:
"{0}" has another command of its kind running at {1}, unseen under the one that began first.
Setting a value at this moment would mean cutting the command that has its way in two here, and the second half would then be hidden by that other command, which changes the picture from here on. So nothing was changed.

Move the playhead to where one of the commands begins or ends and adjust there, or take the overlap away first: drag the commands apart in the timeline, or change their times in the Properties panel.
loop.outside:
The playhead is not within this loop ({0} – {1}).
The commands of a loop repeat in every pass: what the preview adjusts is the moment of the pass the playhead is in, and every pass changes with it.
Move the playhead into the loop and adjust there.

props.bake.step.tip:
osu! has no groups: on export the motion of a group is written as commands of each member, arcs and curves cut into straight pieces.
No piece is cut shorter than this many milliseconds. A larger number means fewer commands; very fast motion then shows its corners.
The preview shows what comes out at this precision, as the game plays it.

How many pixels a position may be off the motion it follows; scale and rotation by as much as comes to the same (0.5 pixels: 0.3% of scale, 0.17° of rotation).
A larger number means fewer commands and a less rounded motion.

props.filter.tip:
When on, the panel shows only the part that is picked in the timeline:
a property row (F opacity, say): its keyframes alone
a loop or trigger: all that is in it
a property row of a loop: the keyframes of that property in that loop
the object itself: everything
When off, the whole object is shown at all times.
Effect row: only that effect’s settings.

Adds or selects this command type at the playhead using the object's current value.
Times count from the start of the loop or trigger; with the playhead ahead of it, the command is added at its start.

Click to select this keyframe; it is highlighted in the timeline, and its property becomes the one that dragging the object in the preview adjusts.

These two kinds of command are in effect at the same time, and osu! lets only one of them have its way.

Several commands of this property run at the same time, so it has no single value at a moment and cannot be shown as keyframes.
The commands can be changed here or in the Script panel.
Where they lie over one another in the timeline, a click selects the shortest, and another click at the same spot the next one.
The property can still be picked and adjusted by dragging in the preview: that changes the command that has its way at the playhead.

props.neverShown: No commands: the object is never shown
props.command.tip: Click to select; the command is highlighted in the timeline

easing.in: Slow at first, then faster and faster.
easing.out: Fast at first, then slower and slower.
easing.inOut: Slow at both ends, fast in between.

easing.bounce.out: Lands and bounces a few times like a ball before it rests.

props.triggerStartTime: Trigger start time (cannot be after the end time)

props.sampleLayer.tip: A sample on the Pass or Fail layer only plays in that state
props.videoTime.tip: The moment the video starts playing; may be negative (the second field of the Video line in the script)
video.commands.tip:
How a video's commands differ from a sprite's:
• Places count from the middle of the picture: M 0,0 is the centre (320,240 for a sprite) and M 100,0 is 100 to the right of it. The last two numbers of the video's line say where it starts.
• Without S the video fills the picture. S sets its size from its own pixels (S 1 = actual size); V scales the size it has. Only one of S and V acts at a time.
• The game always fades a video in over its first second and out over its last. Its own F commands share the opacity with these: of those running, the one that started first acts.
• Its rows have no eye to switch them off, and triggers are not played in the preview.

The pivot of a group can stand anywhere and takes hold of the edges and middle lines of its outline; hold Ctrl to place it freely, and fine-tune it in the properties.
Not available in groups with depth

Select one picture or group, then draw in the preview how it moves:
· Drag to draw a line freehand.
· Or click to place points one by one; Enter or a double click finishes, Backspace takes the last point back, Esc drops them.
The motion starts at the playhead from where the object is. With a Path motion effect selected, the line becomes the effect's path.
Ctrl+click still selects. Not available in groups with depth

Shows the selected difficulty's circles, sliders and spinners between the Foreground and Overlay layers.

viewer.difficulty.tip:
Difficulty shown: {0}
The storyboard of this .osu is drawn together with the shared one (.osb). osu! loads the .osu before the .osb, so the .osu's objects are drawn behind. Background, widescreen and BPM follow this difficulty too.

timeline.snap.tip:
Beat snap divisor. With snapping on, dragging, seeking and creating on the timeline all align to these ticks;
with snapping off, or by typing a time, a time can be off them.
timeline.snapOn.tip:
On: the playhead, bars and keyframes that are dragged, and whatever is created, align to the snap ticks.
Off (free mode): any millisecond will do. Some imported storyboards have their commands at times that are not on a tick; with snapping off those can be dragged a little, and the playhead can stand between two ticks.
The arrow keys go on moving the playhead from tick to tick; to stand exactly on a keyframe, use the previous / next keyframe buttons of the player.
viewer.previousKey.tip:
Go to the previous keyframe (Ctrl+←)
With a property picked, from keyframe to keyframe of that property; otherwise of everything the selected objects or groups have.
The playhead lands exactly on the keyframe, on a tick or not.
viewer.nextKey.tip:
Go to the next keyframe (Ctrl+→)
With a property picked, from keyframe to keyframe of that property; otherwise of everything the selected objects or groups have.
The playhead lands exactly on the keyframe, on a tick or not.

Zoom in a small step, keeping the current time in place.
Alt+wheel (or Ctrl+wheel) over the tracks also zooms the timeline.

Lists only the objects that are being rendered at this moment: sprites and animations whose commands span the current time (also when transparent or off the screen just now), and videos that are playing.
The list follows playback and seeking; the preview stays as it is. Selected objects are always listed. Of Pass and Fail only the layer of the state the preview shows counts; sounds are not listed.
timeline.key.add: Add a keyframe at the playhead
timeline.value.edit: Double-click to edit this keyframe value. Enter confirms; Escape cancels. Separate multiple values with commas.

timeline.track.tip:
Click to pick this property, click again to let go of it.
While it is picked, dragging anywhere in the preview adjusts the selected object at the playhead; hitting its pixels is not required, and a keyframe is added if there is none.
Opacity: drag up and down
Position: drag anywhere (MX only sideways, MY only up and down)
Scale: drag up and down
Vector scale: sideways for the width, up and down for the height
Rotation: up turns clockwise, down anticlockwise

Click to pick this property; click again to let go of it.
Picked, it is what the Properties panel shows alone (while "Show only what is picked" is on).

A group: what is in it, as one thing. Its members stay in the layers they are of, and are shown there in front of what is in no group.
A group higher in the list covers the ones below it: Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ move it up or down, which is how two groups change places.

space.title: Advanced settings
space.intro: With depth (Z, X/Y rotation) or a camera, these decide how members very close to or far from the camera are shown. Distances are measured from the camera along its view, in storyboard pixels.
space.idle: This group has no depth (Z, X/Y rotation) or camera yet, so the settings below do nothing for now.
space.near.tip: A member closer to the camera than Hide is not shown; over the next Fade distance it becomes fully opaque again. This keeps things from suddenly filling the screen as they pass the camera. Written as F (opacity) commands.
space.far.tip:
How members far away disappear:
· Fade: they become transparent, showing what is behind.
· To black: they turn black; suits a black or very dark background. Transparent parts of the picture stay transparent.
Written as F or C (colour) commands; no mask image is added.
space.range.tip: The far effect starts at the From distance and is complete (fully transparent or black) at the Full distance.
space.owner: Space and camera come from the outermost group "{0}".
space.face.tip: Face the camera first, then apply the member’s own rotations.
space.z.tip: Depth: larger is farther away. Members are flat cards at different depths; pictures themselves are never drawn in perspective.
space.rotation.tip: Rotate first around X, then Y, and finally R.
space.dragRefused: Cannot drag: the movement plane is almost edge-on to the camera.

model3d.title: 3D Geometry / Mesh
model3d.layer.tip: Which layer the model is drawn on. New models start on Background, like the built-in templates.
model3d.difficulty.tip: Shared puts the model in the storyboard every difficulty shows; a difficulty puts it in that difficulty's file only.
model3d.import.highFaceCountWarning: Imported 3D mesh has {0} triangles (> 5000); consider setting Max Triangles to simplify.
model3d.points.sampling.tip: Where the points go. Evenly over the surface fills the whole model; along edges draws its outline and sharp edges; rings cuts the model into level slices and lines the points up along them; corners puts one point on each corner of the mesh.
model3d.points.count.tip: How many points the model is made of. Each point is one sprite: more points look fuller but make the storyboard larger and heavier to play.
model3d.points.image.tip: The picture drawn at every point. Leave it empty to use the built-in glowing dot.
model3d.points.size.tip: How wide each point is on the screen. When nearer points are larger, this is the size at the distance the camera looks at.
model3d.points.additive.tip: Points add their light to what is behind them, so overlapping points glow brighter. Turn it off for dark points on a light background.
model3d.points.depthScale.tip: With a perspective camera, points closer to the camera are drawn larger and farther ones smaller.
model3d.points.occlusion.tip: How points on the far side of the model show. Show all makes the model look see-through. Dim the back makes points on surfaces turned away dimmer. Hide behind the model hides points that a nearer part of the model covers; points hidden for a long time are left out of the storyboard.
model3d.fileMissing: The model file is missing from the project's assets. Import the model again.
model3d.loadError: The model file could not be read: {0}
model3d.animation.tip: Which of the model's animations plays. Every moment is worked out and written as ordinary commands.
model3d.animation.speedInvalid: The speed must be greater than 0. The previous speed was kept.
model3d.texture.tip: How the model's textures are shown. Average colour gives each face one colour from its texture. Pictures cuts a small picture from the texture for each half of every face: closer to the texture, but many more pictures and sprites, and a face that turns is split into more sprites as it goes.
space.perspective.tip: Draws the picture truly in perspective: it is cut into cells, and each half of every cell is drawn with a piece of the picture, so a floor or a wall seen at a slant gets smaller into the distance. Off draws it as one sprite, the nearest rectangle to what the camera sees. More cells look closer to the picture, but each cell is four sprites and pieces of picture, and more when the picture turns.
space.dof.tip: The camera is focused on its target. Things that far from the camera stay sharp; nearer or farther they fade or blur. Blur is drawn as copies of each picture blurred in steps, mixed by distance, so it multiplies the sprites of blurred pictures; 3D faces only fade.
space.dof.range.tip: Within the sharp distance in front of and behind the focus, things are sharp. Over the transition after it they fade out completely, or reach the most blur.
space.dof.needsSort: Blur takes effect once Sort by depth is on; until then only fading applies.
space.dof.invalid: The sharp distance cannot be negative, the transition must be greater than 0 and the blur at most 64 pixels. The previous values were kept.
model3d.shadow.tip: Presses the faces lit by the first light flat onto a level ground along that light, and draws them black and see-through below the model. It is an approximation: where the shadows of a shape that is not convex overlap they are darker, and a picture used as the floor should come before the model in the timeline.
